newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty stabilises, market eyes foreign capital flow.
newsitem.headline: Zloty stabilises, market eyes foreign capital flow.

text.p: The zloty temporarily stabilised around one percent above the parity rate in early Friday trade while the market eyed foreign investors whose moves would again set the tone for the day, dealers said.

"The zloty stabilised but whether this will last depends on whether foreign investors want to close further positions or enter into Polish papers after the zloty's Thursday fall," said Mateusz Bieniek, forex dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.
Dealers said the zloty's new short-term range should be between the central bank's enforced resistance level at 1.5 percent above parity and support at parity.
At 0900 GMT the zloty was at 0.98/0.90 percent above parity, softer than the opening's 1.40/1.09 percent but up from morning lows around 0.70 percent.
It was at 3.2610/35 to the dollar, against the opening's 3.2460/560 and at 1.8885/00 to the mark, against 1.8810/70.
Dealers said zloty trade may liven up after the U.S. market opens, with a short-term downside possible, but they remained bullish on the zloty in the longer-term.
They said investments into Poland and the upcoming sale of copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz SA would keep the zloty near the top of its range, unless there were large foreign exits.

"The zloty may weaken further on Friday after U.S. orders come in...but the currency is bound to return to 1.5 percent in the longer term. However, it is unclear what its low will be," said Jerzy Wyjadlowski, forex dealer at Bank Slaski SA.

On Thursday the zloty lost half a percentage point during an estimated $50 million withdrawal of short-term foreign capital from Poland caused by uncertainty about next year's budget and a quickly widening current account deficit.
The money market remained highly volatile on the last trading day of June's reserve period and overnight rates jumped in morning trade after tumbling some six points at the opening.
At 0920 GMT O/N rates were at 22.25/23.60 percent, up from opening's 14.00/18.00 percent, but down from Thursday's close at 23.00/24.10 percent.
Tomorrow/next rates were at 22.10/22.60 percent, straddling the central bank's main 14-day drainage rate of 22.15 percent.
T/N closed at 22.80/24.05 percent on Thursday.
